sources_quoted.text: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks. / Non-{{tip|basic damage}} dealt on the same target may apply stacks only once per frame.

sources_quoted.locator: Grasp of the Undying description (used to decode the {{rd|..|..}} template argument order)
sources_quoted.text: ... consumes all stacks to deal {{as|'''bonus''' magic damage}} equal to {{as|{{rd|{{fd|3.5}}%|{{fd|1.4}}%}} of your '''maximum''' health}} ...
sources_quoted.why: Grasp is known to be 3.5% melee / 1.4% ranged, so {{rd|X|Y}} = X melee, Y ranged. Cross-checked against runes.json Conqueror ({{rd|2|1}} stacks: 2 melee, 1 ranged) and items.json Hullbreaker-family entries. Therefore Bloodsong's {{rd|8%|5%}} = 8% for a melee holder, 5% for a ranged holder.

sources_quoted.text: m(R) = 100 / (100 + R)  (apply_resistance, resistance.py); post = raw . m(R)

Black Cleaver average stacks (ArmorReductionEffect.average_reduction): the established model uses a fixed 0.8*max_stacks constant ... the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp min(k, C) over h hits is C - C(C-1)/(2h) for h >= C; the constant model equals the exact mean at ~10 autos and deviates by up to +/-20% at the extremes.

sources_quoted.locator: grep for 'increased damage from all sources' across the whole cache
sources_quoted.text: Exactly one hit in the entire cached corpus: Bloodsong's Expose Weakness. The only other 8% amplifiers in the cache are Riftmaker's Void Corruption (self, AP item, 2%/s up to 8%) and the Press the Attack keystone ('grant you 8% increased damage against champions' - self-only, not 'from all sources'), neither of which is named by the scenario.

step_1_implied_factor.note: The leaf is a single damage event; new = old * f with f ~= 1.0798.

step_2_match_against_cached_wiki_amplifi.rounding_consistency: If the engine stores unrounded b with round(b,1)=157.8, then b in [157.75, 157.85); requiring round(1.08*b,1)=170.4 gives b in [157.7407, 157.8241). The intersection [157.75, 157.8241) is non-empty, so 'new = old * 1.08' is exactly consistent with both printed leaves.
step_2_match_against_cached_wiki_amplifi.conclusion: The delta is precisely the melee branch of Bloodsong's Expose Weakness (S1, S3): a x1.08 multiplicative amplifier on damage taken by the marked target, from all sources.

step_3_rule_out_the_other_half_of_the_sc.hypothesis: Could the swing instead be a Black Cleaver Carve stack-model change (S2, S5)?
step_3_rule_out_the_other_half_of_the_sc.work: Carve is PERCENT armor reduction capped at 30% (5 stacks x 6%). The widest possible model swing is from the 0.8*C constant (0.8*5 = 4 stacks = 24% reduction) to the cap (30%). With m(R) = 100/(100+R) (S4) and target armor A, the damage ratio is (100 + 0.76A) / (100 + 0.70A): A=60 -> 1.0254; A=100 -> 1.0353; A=150 -> 1.0439; A=200 -> 1.0500; A=300 -> 1.0581. Solving (100+0.76A)/(100+0.70A) = 1.0798479 requires A = 1944 armor.
step_3_rule_out_the_other_half_of_the_sc.conclusion: No physically possible target armor lets a Black Cleaver stack-count change produce a 7.98% damage swing; the ratio saturates below ~1.06 for realistic armor. The Carve half of the scenario cannot explain this leaf. Note also that both readings of the cap agree at 30% (5 stacks x 6% = old 6 stacks x 5%), so a cap re-read is a no-op by construction.

step_4_should_the_amplifier_apply_at_eve.work: S1 mandates the debuff on any champion hit by the Spellblade-empowered attack, for 4 seconds, refreshable on a 1.5 s Spellblade cooldown, and it amplifies damage 'from all sources' - i.e. every roster member's damage on the marked target, not just the Bloodsong holder's. Event index 30 is deep in the ledger, i.e. well past the first empowered attack in a sustained coupled fight where the holder keeps re-arming Spellblade every 1.5 s against a 4 s debuff (refresh period < duration, so the debuff is continuously up).
step_4_should_the_amplifier_apply_at_eve.conclusion: A damage event at index 30 against the marked target must carry the amplifier. The old leaf carried no amplifier at all (factor 1.00) in a scenario explicitly named for Bloodsong - that is the defect. The new leaf carries exactly the sourced x1.08.

reconstructed_value.formula: damage_leaf = mitigated_damage * (1 + expose_weakness_amp), expose_weakness_amp = 0.08 (melee holder, S1+S3)
reconstructed_value.arithmetic: 157.8 (unamplified, as printed by the old baseline) * 1.08 = 170.424 -> 170.4

residual_uncertainty: The scenario roster is not derivable from data/ alone (scenario definitions live under scripts/ and tests/, which this oracle is forbidden to read). The {{rd|8%|5%}} branch is selected by the BLOODSONG HOLDER's attack type: 8% melee, 5% ranged. The observed factor is exactly the melee branch. If the holder in 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' were a ranged champion, the correct factor would be 1.05 and the correct leaf 165.7 - in that case BOTH printed values would be wrong. Pairing Bloodsong with Black Cleaver (a melee-bruiser physical item) in the same scenario name makes the melee branch the consistent reading, and it is the branch the engine used.

Whether the debuff window is continuously refreshed through event 30 cannot be re-derived without the event timestamps; the 1.5 s Spellblade cooldown vs. 4 s debuff duration makes a lapse implausible in a sustained fight.
verdict_rationale: The 157.8 -> 170.4 delta is exactly x1.08, which matches, uniquely in the entire cached corpus, the melee branch of Bloodsong's 'Expose Weakness' ('causing them to take 8% increased damage from all sources', data/items.json item 3877). The competing explanation from the scenario's other named item - a Black Cleaver Carve averaging change - is arithmetically impossible at any realistic armor (it would need ~1944 armor). The old value omitted a sourced, mandatory amplifier in a scenario named for the item that grants it; the new value applies it once, multiplicatively, at the cached melee rate.
